problem:
A metal structure of mass $2500\,\text{kg}$ is released vertically downward with an initial velocity of $4\,\text{m/s}.$ Let $v(t)$ be the structure's velocity, in meters per second, $t\ge 0$ seconds after release, with downward taken as the positive direction. The air resistance on the structure is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=39.2\,\text{kg/m}$ and acts in the direction opposite to motion.

Find, rounded to two decimal places, the velocity of the structure after $1$ second.
Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the structure are the weight due to gravity and drag.

activity_context.topic_title: Falling Body Problems With Quadratic Drag
